gen-gf-agu-display-fs-rowan: Bent-wire letters with a bold, odd charm lead the way. Rowan follows in a classic serif with friendly curves, and it is the one built for sustained reading, not for long paragraphs of the heading.
gen-gf-akaya-kanadaka-fs-rowan: Pulled-back terminals and tightly knit spacing give Akaya Kanadaka its commanding look. Rowan is the gentler one, with openings in every curve and a literary warmth that suits brief copy better than the display face.
gen-gf-akaya-telivigala-fs-rowan: Crowded glyphs strung like beads give Akaya Telivigala its look, with a wide bracelet-like c. And Rowan, a text serif with friendly curves, keeps a longer passage moving, though it isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-aladin-fs-paquito: Commanding is how Aladin comes across, its pen never shifting pressure or angle across tight, filled-in words. And Paquito, with little gap between lowercase and caps, loosens things up, handy for a handful of lines.
gen-gf-alkatra-fs-rowan: Bold, with strokes sitting between monoline and hairline, Alkatra takes the top spot. Rowan, a classic serif with open curves, settles into the page gently and is comfortable in small doses.
gen-gf-allan-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, with a lightly shaded texture running through each word. And Allan, hugged tight with a matching crossbar and stem on its t, gives way to it for a handful of lines.
gen-gf-amita-fs-amulya: Amita writes in rounded, dowel-like strokes that stay open and inviting. And Amulya, modern with generous curves, gives that relaxed hand a tidy partner, better for brief copy.
gen-gf-amita-fs-neco: Relaxed handwriting up top meets dignified type below. Neco, a text serif with a light swelling from hairline to stem, keeps a longer passage steady and good for a handful of lines.
gen-gf-amita-fs-plein: Amita traces its letters like one marker, with no pressure swell where curves turn a corner, so keep Plein modest in size. Plein stays clean.
gen-gf-amita-fs-recia: Amita bends its letters like a paperclip, friendly and relaxed, with no thick-thin shifts anywhere. Recia stays sturdy and sharp, though.
